## noun

open·​ing

ˈōp-niŋ, 

ˈō-pə- 

Synonyms of opening

Simple Definition A Simple Definition is available from our Learner's Dictionary to help you understand the meaning faster.

1

a

: an act or instance of making or becoming open

b

: an act or instance of beginning : commencement

especially : a formal and usually public event by which something new is put officially into operation

2

: something that is open: such as

a(1)

: breach, aperture

(2)

: an open width : span

a three-inch opening

b

: an area without trees or with scattered usually mature trees that occurs as a break in a forest

c

: two pages that face one another in a book

3

: something that constitutes a beginning: such as

a

: a usually planned series of moves made at the beginning of a game of chess or checkers compare endgame, middle game

b

: a first performance

attended the play's opening

4

a

: occasion, chance

She was waiting for an opening to tell her story.

b

: an opportunity for employment

The department has several openings.

#### Continuous Adoration in the Blessed Sacrament Chapel

From Monday to Saturday, at the end of the 8:30 a.m. Mass, the Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament takes place. Eucharistic Adoration in the Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament continues uninterrupted throughout the day and concludes with the Eucharistic Benediction at the end of the day.

Visits, with a guide provided by the Fabbrica di San Pietro or with your own guide, can be done

- Monday to Saturday, from 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. (last registration at 5 p.m.);
- Sundays and Vatican holidays, from 1.30 p.m. to 3.30 p.m. (last registration at 3 p.m.).

#### Hours Historical Archive of the Fabbrica di San Pietro

The Historical Archive of the Fabbrica di San Pietro is open from 15 September to 15 July.

The study room is accessible from Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

A dedicated access path is reserved for worshippers and celebrants. They are therefore invited to present themselves at the indicated entrance gate for the identification. Once outside, anyone wishing to visit the Basilica may do so at a later time by re-entering through the standard entrances.

【turn18news8】 [wordlim: 100] Published: 9 months ago; Brian and Martha Johnson, founders of the Johnson and Johnson Mobile Veterinary Clinic, have opened a new brick-and-mortar veterinary clinic in Jacksonville, Illinois. Established in August 2023, their mobile service has been active across west-central Illinois, including towns like Pittsfield, White Hall, and Winchester. The new clinic, located at 610 N. Prairie St., provides a home base while maintaining mobile service routes. The facility aims to offer more immediate care to clients in Jacksonville and accommodate those needing services when the mobile unit is unavailable locally.

The Johnsons, both veterinary graduates—Martha from the University of Missouri and Brian from the University of Illinois—were inspired by a desire to serve the community and build a legacy for their daughter, Ayla. Currently the only veterinarians at their clinic, they employ several vet techs and hope to hire a third vet soon. The clinic has experienced increasing demand since opening, with a ribbon-cutting scheduled for January 5 and a grand opening celebration planned in the spring. The clinic operates Monday through Friday with varying hours each day.
Mobile veterinarians open Jacksonville clinic, keep routes running
Date: Fri Dec 26 10:50:11 2025 UTC

A couple that has been providing mobile veterinarian services across west-central Illinois is putting down additional roots with a brick-and-mortar clinic in Jacksonville.
Brian and Martha Johnson created their Johnson and Johnson Mobile Veterinary Clinic in August 2023 and since have had stops in Jacksonville.
It has been about a year and a half since they announced their new clinic building, but renovations had to be completed before the clinic could open at 610 N. Prairie St.
"We are very excited," Martha Johnson said. "It has always been my dream to open my own clinic, so it's nice seeing that come to fruition."
The site will provide a permanent home base for the clinic.
The mobile clinic serves Pittsfield, White Hall, Waverly, Hardin, Winchester and other locations throughout the week. Those mobile locations will remain active, with the Jacksonville site simply a permanent location open to all.
"We saw a need in Jacksonville and this allows us to serve out clients who need more prompt care," Brian Johnson said. "Having a location here allows clients of our mobile clinic to bring in their pets here if they need an appointment but the mobile clinic is in a town farther away."
They hope this location is an opportunity for their clinic to grow.
While the Johnsons are the clinic's only veterinarians, they have several vet techs and hope to bring on a third veterinarian soon.
"We have gotten busier and busier every day we've been set up here, so we know there is a need," Brian Johnson said. 
The hope is to build something their daughter, 3-month-old Ayla, can be proud of when she is older, they said, calling her their inspiration.
"Maybe one day she'll join the family business," Brian Johnson said. "She will be growing up here after all."
Both veterinarians attended undergraduate school at Truman State University, where they met. Martha Johnson then graduated from the University of Missouri and Brian Johnson graduated from the University of Illinois, both with degrees in veterinary medicine. 
After graduating, they moved to the area and worked in a traditional veterinary clinic for about a year before venturing out on their own to establish the mobile clinic. 
A ribbon-cutting ceremony for the brick-and-mortar clinic will be at 9:30 a.m. Jan. 5, with the hope of having a bigger grand-opening ceremony in the spring to allow the community to come in, take a look around and meet them.
